MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JUNE 13, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:12 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Dancers from the Elite Dance Studio led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PRESENTATION TO TIM THOMAS, FORMER PLANNING COMMISSIONER, IN
  RECOGNITION OF HIS SERVICE TO THE CITY

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commented that it was her pleasure to present former
  Park and Activities and Planning Commissioner Tim Thomas with a plaque
  thanking him for his service to the City over the last several years.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL also thanked Mr. Thomas noting her appreciation
  for his fresh ideas and willingness to work at City events.

  Mr. Thomas thanked the COUNCIL and expressed his appreciation for
  everyone’s support.

B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR'S FREE RESIDENTIAL
  REFUSE SERVICE

  Sharon Shapiro-Fox and Angela Dulce, Waste Management Representatives,
  drew the name of Stella Hyatt on Saddlehorn Lane for one year’s free refuse
  service.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 23, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 23, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 13, 2017
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS - MAY AND JUNE

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 58472 THROUGH 58506 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $392,764.34; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050117 THROUGH 050217;
  57824 (VOID); 58133 (VOID); 58340 THROUGH 54347; 58380
  THROUGH 58409; 58406 (VOID); 58443 THROUGH 58462; 58448
  THROUGH 58450 (VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF $221,196.28 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $613,960.62 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A AND B.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

  APPROVED.

  THAT CAN BEGIN FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30, 2017. THE

COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN pulled Item 6C for discussion.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF SO ORDERED.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Planning Director Wahba noted
  that staff is looking into creating sign brightness standards as recommended by
  Planning Commissioner Scott as well as with the Applicant (TKM Investment
  Company).

B.  MC GOWAN CONSULTING LLC PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR
  MS4 PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with McGowan Consulting LLC for MS4 Permit compliance
  assistance for FY 2017-18 in an amount not to exceed $88,630.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting LLC, provided an extensive overview
  of the work plan for the coming year.

  Ms. McGowan then responded to various questions posed by the COUNCIL.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Ms. McGowan noted an
  educational outreach will be provided to the residents regarding compliance
  with specific requirements that must be met.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Ms. McGowan noted that the
  Graphic Design and Website Layout is being coordinated with the Bay Cities
  Watershed Group through the South Bay Energy Service Center. She further
  noted that they will post information on integrated waste management as well
  as provide educational outreach on their website and also provide a brochure to
  include material for construction sites informing them of the requirements.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired as to how often Nationwide Street
  Sweeping cleans the streets. Assistant City Manager Grammer responded that
  they are swept twice a month.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL then inquired if that was enough to meet the
  requirements. Ms. McGowan noted that sweeping twice a month does meet the
  requirements and that the City will be monitoring trash in areas where storm
  drains cannot be retrofitted. She further noted that if trash is found at those
  locations, then it may make sense to increase the City’s street sweeping routine.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the City is going through the process
  of cleaning and updating the storm drains and this may assist in alleviating the
  storm drain problems.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 13, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that Ms. McGowan was working with the
  City of Torrance, but apparently that is no longer an option. Ms. McGowan
  then commented that the Peninsula Watershed Group is pursuing less
  expensive projects to address the Machado Lake pollutant limits, but are facing
  some challenges. She noted that the Peninsula cities are still looking to
  coordinate with the City of Torrance and perhaps the Sanitation Districts to
  identify other opportunities. Additionally, she reported that she and staff
  members from the Peninsula cities recently toured the rehabilitated Machado
  Lake and are working with the City of Los Angeles.

  Ms. McGowan acknowledged COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN’S participation with
  the League of California Cities and California Contract Cities Association on
  storm water funding options.

  Ms. McGowan was pleased to note that Santa Monica Bay beaches on the
  Peninsula are mostly being “de-listed” as impaired. She further noted that the
  Regional Board also recommended that the Wilmington Drain be de-listed for
  copper and lead, but the new challenge for Santa Monica Bay will be arsenic
  and mercury affecting fish which they hope to collect data ahead of the process.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired if the equestrian community has been
  engaged in this process.  Ms. McGowan noted that three of the larger
  horsekeeping facilities were contacted a few years ago, but they can certainly
  revisit this issue and reach out again to the equestrians.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested that an article be placed in the City’s
  newsletter regarding best management practices.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented that one of her concerns is a lack of
  education to the public on how to treat overgrown vegetation. She noted that
  an individual sprayed chemicals on the hillside in her neighborhood and this
  was not acceptable. She further noted that those residents who attend the
  Earth Day event are familiar with the problems, but others are not aware of the
  environmental impacts this causes. She asked if education could be provided
  on how to maintain landscaping through organic means. Ms. McGowan
  responded that she could bring this matter to the Watershed Group for their
  input.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that information could also be posted on
  the City’s social media sites.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ emphasized that this is very important for all the
  residents.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that there is an upcoming county-wide
  election which could generate additional funding and provide options as well as
  opportunities for cost-sharing.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  MCGOWAN CONSULTING LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT COMPLIANCE
  ASSISTANCE FOR FY 2017-18 IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED
  $88,630.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

C.  PROPOSAL FOR PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM REPORT UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the proposal from Willdan
  Engineering and contract agreement to provide professional engineering
  consultant services to prepare a 2017 Pavement Management System Report
  Update in the amount of $30,000.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 13, 2017
   In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that the report will be provided by Willdan and brought back to the
  COUNCIL at the end of September.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO APPROVE THE PROPOSAL FROM WILLDAN ENGINEERING AND
  CONTRACT AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING
  CONSULTANT SERVICES TO PREPARE A 2017 PAVEMENT
  MANAGEMENT SYSTEM REPORT UPDATE IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $30,000.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

D.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 719 AMENDING AND RESTATING
  CHAPTER 5.04 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO BUSINESS LICENSING

  Recommendation:  That the City Council introduce Ordinance No. 719,
  amending and restating Chapter 5.04 of the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal
  Code pertaining to business licensing.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He noted
  that a letter was submitted by an individual from the Palos Verdes Peninsula
  Chamber of Commerce listing their concerns that this would place an additional
  burden on them for the PV Street Fair.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that a principal of a particular event would
  apply for a business license rather than having staff collect individual license
  fees.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained the process noting that it
  is not uncommon in other cities to follow the same procedure for a one-time
  event. He noted that the City and Chamber have done this in the past, but it
  changed when they decided on another method. He further noted that the fee
  of $36 could be added to the entrance fee making it easier to manage, but
  oftentimes there was a lack of communication between the Chamber and City
  regarding the updated vendor list which necessitated staff to attend the Street
  Fair and track down those vendors who did not submit a business license.
  Finally, he noted that the proposed ordinance would streamline the process.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF referred to the aforementioned letter noting that it
  mentioned the Chamber was disappointed at not being consulted about this
  agenda item.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that staff will reach out to the Chamber
  to address their concerns and explain the intent of the ordinance.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ took exception to the comment that the Chamber
  was not advised of this meeting and stated that it is incumbent upon citizens to
  review the agendas as they are posted on the website prior to every meeting.
  She noted that the City also supports the Street Fair and reiterated that this
  item was not scheduled at the last minute since it had been discussed in prior
  meetings.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that this proposal is advantageous to the
  Chamber and would be done in a unified way. He further noted that if the City
  thought this was not favorable to the Chamber, staff would have reached out to
  them, but this was not the case.

  City Attorney Davis noted that the key word is “may” as mentioned in the
  Ordinance.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 13, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 719, AMENDING AND RESTATING
  CHAPTER 5.04 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO BUSINESS LICENSING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

  Assistant City Manager Grammer read Ordinance No. 719 by title only.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AMENDMENT TO THE PROPOSAL TO CONDUCT AN INITIAL STUDY AND
  MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION FOR THE PALOS VERDES PIPELINE
  PROJECT; APPLICANT:  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICES COMPANY (CAL
  WATER); LOCATION: VARIOUS LOCATIONS CITY-WIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the First Amendment to the
  PSA with ESA/PCR in the amount of $9,380 to complete the Initial Study and
  resulting, appropriate environmental determination for the Palos Verdes
  Pipeline Project.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

   COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that good discussion took place regarding
  the recent Mayor’s Breakfast Ride and how to better address equestrian
  participation. First, she stated that she did receive different perspectives from
  the Committee Members and one concern was the early time which posed a
  problem for those who have to ready their horses for the ride. Secondly, she
  suggested that prior to the ride, schedule a coffee “meet and greet” event with
  COUNCIL MEMBERS and then proceed at 9:00 a.m. She further noted that
  discussion continued regarding not including carriages as they tend to spook
  the horses and would like to explore this further.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN emphasized that some of the guests, i.e. elected
  officials, may wish to ride in the carriage and would not like to see this
  eliminated. COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ stressed that equestrians tend to stay
  away because of the commotion the carriage causes as it makes the horses very
  uncomfortable.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also mentioned the lack of horses available for the
  recent ride and would like to see that improved for next year. COUNCILMAN
  ZUCKERMAN suggested that perhaps the City can rent horses.

  After further discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO START THE COFFEE MEET AND GREET AT 8:30 A.M. AT
  CHANDLER PARK AND THE MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE AT 9:00 A.M.
  AND CONSIDER RENTING HORSES FOR NEXT YEAR’S EVENT.
